## Design

### 2026-10-23 – I did the project's schematic. I designed the main design and schematic for the project.  It is  going to be a small drum set, with 8 touch sensitive buttons, and a speaker for playing the audio. It w

**1.5h**

I did the project's schematic. I designed the main design and schematic for the project.  It is  going to be a small drum set, with 8 touch sensitive buttons, and a speaker for playing the audio. It will be controlled by a XIAO ESP32-S3. I chose this microcontroller, because it is small, let's me use touch sensitive buttons, and has enough power to play the audio.Here's my drawing of how it will fit together:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/sDE0sWuzf8SaPJwrIDtc043sSoi90nZ7/9109d12664cdd045e89fb5c2cafdbafef9fe3e62da38058a53902ffe2b14ce18.png)

After that I did the schematic. Nothing really special, it was a pretty straigthforward process:

![Screenshot from 2026-10-22 16-44-25](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/sDE0sWuzf8SaPJwrIDtc043sSoi90nZ7/b4b4d43c4510039d37af33f59bcb91c83700e8d4088e3f0182a0b8ee791791df.png)

I did the PCB. I first did the custom footprint for the buttons, which wasn't too easy, because I had to make it smaller than 100mm in order to fit within the budget. In the end, after like 2 other versions I ended up with this:

**3h**

I finished the PCB, and made the CAD model. First the PCB: I made a cutout on the right side up top to be able to fit the speaker up there. I also added mounting holes, added some filets, and expiramented a bit with the silkscreen. Here is how the final layout turned out:

I also assigned 3D models for the part's that needed it, here is the finished 3D model:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/sDE0sWuzf8SaPJwrIDtc043sSoi90nZ7/a88aa59ee2db3fc04fda06f424bb7101724360c48ffeabcaf28de1f246aa79c8.png)

### 2026-10-25 – I did the finishing touches, and got everything ready for submission. First I had done the firmware, but I tracked that with hackatime, so I won't include that here, but it went pretty smoothly with t

**1.5h**

I did the finishing touches, and got everything ready for submission. First I had done the firmware, but I tracked that with hackatime, so I won't include that here, but it went pretty smoothly with the docs. I also tracked writing the README with hackatime, so that is also not included in this devlog. One thing that the hackatime did not include,  was choosing the sounds to play with the ESP32,  which I did by downloading a sound pack that was thankfully fully free, and didn't require any credits, but then I had to select a sound for each type of drum, which was pretty complicated, since I know nothing about drums, and the filenames weren't helping too much. After I got that sorted I did the README, and got the gerbers for the PCB. To  save on costs, I downloaded JLCPCB's app, which got like 5$ off the BOM, so that was definetly appreciated.

![Screenshot from 2026-10-25 19-38-14](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/sDE0sWuzf8SaPJwrIDtc043sSoi90nZ7/e833de457f5ed71a8fdc55948c6a6ea8546e4bb2a28a696bf6182523e3c7d7ef.png)

After that I also did some changes in the Aliexpress order, which was a bit less complicated, but still not the easiest.

![Screenshot from 2026-10-25 20-32-53](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/sDE0sWuzf8SaPJwrIDtc043sSoi90nZ7/1188763acfab386cb3050c11579ff617aaa291a33d62e97459e66b799a3af6f0.png)

 But now finally, I think I'm ready for submission!
